name: Central Fund of Israel
subtitle: Conduit / pass-through · $109,179,379 revenue, 2024
what_the_record_says: Conduit / pass-through. Jurisdiction as recorded: Cedarhurst, NY, USA. Financial conduit for Israeli groups soliciting US donations. Its own FY2023 Schedule F states 438 recipient organisations outside the US that year (OCR-read directly from the filed Form 990, ProPublica pdf_url below); the schedule's line-item detail naming each recipient is not present in this PDF rendering, so the 438 figure is confirmed but the specific foreign recipients behind it mostly are not (Israel Land Fund and Ateret Cohanim, both already in this table on other sourcing, are known exceptions). Its FY2021 Schedule F (a separate, readable filing, verified by direct visual inspection of the rendered page, not OCR inference) shows this is CFI's actual disclosure practice, not a one-off PDF gap: all ~94 foreign/Israeli grant line items across 76 pages leave the '(a) Name of organization' field blank, disclosing only region ('Middle East') and a purpose category (humanitarian aid, medical aid, security, religious, legal aid, youth at risk, women's health, public awareness), totalling roughly $18.9 million that year with no recipient named anywhere in the filing. Its FY2021 Schedule I (US-domestic grants) DOES name recipients, including American Friends of Elon Moreh - a direct settlement-funding vehicle, see F017 - alongside general-purpose domestic grantees such as the Zionist Organization of America ($200,000), Center for Freedom and Safety ($200,000) and Friedman Center for Peace Through Strength ($250,000), which illustrates that CFI is a broad-purpose conduit and a grant from it does not by itself establish a settlement link - only a named, settlement-specific grant does. Total expenses grew from $36.7M (2019) to $96.1M (2024) Official action: T'ruah complaint (2015) prompted IRS criminal investigation; closed without charges This rests on a primary filing.

name: Christian Friends of Israeli Communities (CFOIC)
subtitle: Direct funder

IRS classifies it NTEE X99 (Religion-Related) rather than the Q or T codes carried by every other US entity in this table; it is not a synagogue or congregation - it is not a place of worship, and files as an independent international support organisation - so it is included on the same conduct standard as every other row here: a body that itself names which settlements it funds.
